newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power prices flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power prices flat to lower.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West were flat to slightly lower Friday amid cooler temperatures and expectations for rain in the Northwest, market sources said.
"The weather is cooling off and some units are coming back," noted one trader.
Temperatures in California and other areas have returned to seasonally normal levels, but parts of Arizona are forecast to continue seeing above-normal temperatures through early next week.
California-Oregon border (COB) power for Monday and Tuesday was last quoted at $19.00-19.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), little changed from Thursday.

The Bonneville Power Administration left its non-firm price offers for Monday and Tuesday unchanged at $18.50 per MWh for Northwest deliveries during heavy-load hours and at $20.00 for the California border.
Next-day Palo Verde was last quoted at $19.00-20.00 per MWh, down from $19.50-21.00 on Wednesday.
